calls.head: The Predators want Marchessault away from the big guns
calls.body: At home, the Predators keep sending Marchessault’s line (Schaefer, Kerfoot and Marchessault) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Mammoth’s fourth line is O'Brien, Stenlund and But.

calls.head: The Mammoth are likely to tilt the ice
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Mammoth have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Predators near the bottom. The ice is likely to tilt the Mammoth’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

NSH.head: We had Nashville as slight underdogs (42%), and it went Utah’s way.

UTA.head: We leaned Utah’s way (58%), and they came through.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Keller sparks a Mammoth comeback
paras: The first period was a wild one. Filip Forsberg opened the scoring for the Predators just 52 seconds into the game, and Roman Josi extended the lead to 2-0 shorthanded late in the period. Clayton Keller and Mikhail Sergachev scored less than two minutes apart later in the period to tie it 2-2. Anders Lee gave the Mammoth the lead late in the second. There were five goals in the third period alone. Alexander Kerfoot tied it up for Nashville early in the period, in his first game against Utah since leaving. Lawson Crouse restored the Mammoth’s lead a little over four minutes later, but Ross Colton tied it 4-4 for Nashville 49 seconds later. Nashville had a goal taken off for a missed stoppage midway through the third. Mavrik Bourque gave the Preds the lead later in the period. Lee scored his second of the night with just under four minutes left to tie it 5-5. That disallowed goal stung: the game went to a shootout, and Trocheck scored the only goal of the shootout to win it for the Mammoth. MacKenzie Weegar finished with three assists.

The Mammoth owned the chances, outshooting the Predators 35-21, and still had to sweat it out in a shootout. The Predators hit two posts and still lost. Karel Vejmelka made 16 saves for the Mammoth, and Juuse Saros stopped 30 of 35 at the other end. The Mammoth moved to 14-10-3, seventh in the Central, while the Predators dropped to 13-6-6 but climbed to third in the Central.

items.text: Vincent Trocheck has a point in six straight games.
Dylan Guenther extended his point streak against Nashville to seven games.
The Mammoth won without Nate Schmidt, John Marino, Michael Carcone and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team was missing more at the time.
The Mammoth’s Gregor Biber played his first NHL game.
